topic: ROUND THREE of the overengineering lane: five bounded iterations on angles the first two rounds covered thinly or not at all. Context: the whole system-spec-kit skill as a size-and-value question.

focus: KQ-R3a: validator-registry rows 1-12 — defect class, sibling/template overlap, test-name coverage per row (header comments only)
noveltyJustification: Prior rounds never compared rule rows against each other by defect class: round one explicitly skipped rule bodies, round two checked orphan-ness and inventory claims, not row-vs-row overlap. The FILE_EXISTS/LEVEL_MATCH and FRONTMATTER_MEMORY_BLOCK/FRONTMATTER_VALID class-level overlaps, and the stale L1/L3-only header table in check-files.sh, were unrecorded. Both overlaps are candidates pending iteration 2's row 19/21 reads.
keyQuestions: KQ-R3a: which of rows 1-12 catch a defect class no sibling or template catches, and which have neither a distinguishing class nor a test?
answeredQuestions: KQ-R3a (partially): all 12 rows have >=1 test file naming the id and no row 1-12 has both an overlapping sibling and no test; two class-level overlap candidates and one stale header found (F3-01..F3-03); behavioral confirmation of F3-01/F3-02 delegated to iteration 2

ruledOut.approach: Re-reporting census-kept AC pair / level-declared / ts five-rule family (F6, F8)
ruledOut.reason: census marks them kept with documented reasons; no new evidence contradicting those reasons

ruledOut.approach: Reading rule bodies beyond header comments
ruledOut.reason: mandate: header comments only for rows 1-12 in this iteration

statement: FILE_EXISTS ('Validates required spec documents for the declared documentation level') and LEVEL_MATCH ('Checks required files match the declared documentation level') name the same defect class in the registry while running different scripts (check-files.sh vs check-level-match.sh, the latter sourcing utils/template-structure.js).
cost: two authored_template rows + two scripts + two test surfaces maintained for one apparent defect; a reader cannot tell the split from the registry

statement: Two frontmatter validators: the ts row validates canonical _memory continuity frontmatter blocks, the script row validates YAML frontmatter structure and required semantic values — same document zone, disjointness undocumented.
cost: two rule surfaces over one zone; if disjoint, the split is invisible to a reader

statement: Header enumerates only 'Level 1: spec.md, plan.md, tasks.md' and 'Level 3: Level 2 + decision-record.md' — no Level 2 line and no mention of acceptance-criteria.md, the post-011 closure doc that distinguishes L2+.
cost: reader-facing comment misrepresents the level table; if the body also omits the closure doc, the rule is wrong

focus: KQ-R3b: validator-registry rows 13-39 — family judgment (graph-metadata, canonical-save, acceptance), header comments only, 12 reads
noveltyJustification: Prior rounds audited rule bodies for orphans and inventory claims but never judged the metadata family as one: the strict bridge re-implementing three shell rows' invariants over the same two JSON files, six rows with zero naming tests, the header-convention violation in check-spec-doc-integrity.sh (row 29), the anchor dual-validator split, and the expired 2026-05-01 grandfather windows in check-canonical-save.sh are all unrecorded. F3-02 resolved toward 'undocumented split'; F3-01 gained the missing evidence (LEVEL_MATCH header has no description block).
keyQuestions: KQ-R3b: what do the graph-metadata, canonical-save and acceptance families each catch, and are internal members redundant with each other?
answeredQuestions: KQ-R3b (family judgment): children trio coherent; canonical-save keep holds (F8) with expired-window signal (F3-09); metadata family redundant at 8 rows/2 files (F3-04); 6 rows zero-naming-tests (F3-06); anchor dual validator (F3-07); identity/drift test asymmetry (F3-08)

ruledOut.reason: census recorded the deliberate keep; header re-read confirms per-row attribution still the stated reason

statement: Metadata family is 8 rows over 2 files (description.json, graph-metadata.json): the strict bridge re-validates through the shared schemas plus path-prefix/status-enum invariants, while three shell rows independently validate shape (graph, description) and the disk-path identity invariant.
cost: 3 shell scripts + 1 TS bridge + 8 registry rows maintaining overlapping invariants over two small generated files

statement: The row-29 script has no Rule/Severity/Description comment block, no 'Sourced by validate.sh' line and no rule id in its header — unlike every sibling — and its first substantive line shells to git rev-parse.
cost: reader cannot match the script to its registry row from the code itself; convention drift inside the rule corpus

statement: Six rule ids have zero test files naming them: TOC_POLICY, AI_PROTOCOLS, GRAPH_METADATA_CHILD_IDENTITY, DESCRIPTION_SHAPE, SPEC_DOC_INTEGRITY, IMPROVEMENT_ARTIFACTS; 33 of 39 rows have at least one.
cost: 6 of 39 rules cannot be located from tests by id (coverage measurement is id-string based; behavior tests might exist without the string — caveat recorded)

statement: ANCHORS_VALID (native orchestrator, 7 test files) validates anchor syntax/pairing/order/uniqueness; GREP_CONVENTION's scan also includes 'anchor grammar' (1 test file) — two surfaces for one defect, split by execution layer only.
cost: two anchor validators whose headers never name each other

statement: The error-severity member of the children_ids pair (stale rename residue the writer never prunes) has 0 naming tests while its warn+flag sibling has 1.
cost: the check guarding the invariant that cannot self-heal is the least-tested

statement: Grandfathering comments state 'allowlist expires at 2026-05-01T00:00:00Z' and 'save_lineage enforcement becomes hard ... on/after 2026-05-01T00:00:00Z'; today is 2026-09-07 — if the body still executes the time branches they are 4-month-dead code, if graduated the comment is stale.
cost: rolled-out deadline scaffolding not verified by any prior round; dead-branch risk or stale doc
recommendation: merge (graduate or delete the window branch)

focus: KQ-R3c: step sequences repeated across the /speckit:* command assets (steps only, 8 files)
noveltyJustification: Prior rounds audited the command assets' checklist content (census §4, fixed in 011) but never compared the step graphs to each other: complete as the union of plan+implement, save_context as the only step in all three workflows (6 duplicated copies, two placeholder conventions), 14 validate.sh --strict invocations across 3 workflows (7 in complete alone), and the auto/confirm twins were all unrecorded.
keyQuestions: KQ-R3c: which step sequences are duplicated across commands, and is any command's body a subset of another's?
answeredQuestions: KQ-R3c: plan 1-4 == complete 1-4; implement 2-3-5-6-7 == complete 7-8-9-10-12; save_context in all three; no command is a strict subset of another (complete adds acceptance_criteria + acceptance_verify + 2 autopilot steps)

ruledOut.approach: Calling complete a strict subset of plan+implement
ruledOut.reason: complete adds acceptance_criteria/acceptance_verify/autopilot steps — union, not subset

statement: Complete's 16 steps: 12 names exist in plan (1-4 plus planning) or implement (task_breakdown..completion) with identical order — only acceptance_criteria, acceptance_verify and the autopilot steps are unique.
cost: every contract change (like 011's) edited 8 assets separately; three copies of two lifecycles to keep coherent
protects: nothing unique to the duplicated steps

statement: save_context (the generate-context.js node) is a step in all three lifecycle commands, duplicated in 6 files under two handover names, with two placeholder conventions for the same argument ({spec_path} in plan vs [spec-folder-path] in implement/complete).
cost: 6 copies of the continuity-writer invocation contract; placeholder drift already occurred between copies

statement: The identical full 39-rule gate is invoked 14 times across the three workflows (7 within complete alone), each re-validating the same folder after a different write; no note explains the cadence.

protects: progressive validation (if each site guards a distinct write — unverified)

statement: Plan, implement and complete each maintain two near-identical 700-1300-line assets differing only in present_options_to_user insertion points (resume's confirm variant genuinely differs).

location: system-spec-kit/SKILL.md:95 (typed leaf projection paragraph) vs leaf-manifest.json (45 paths) vs SKILL.md:167ff RESOURCE_MAP (26 unique paths)
statement: Claimed: 'every one is enumerated in leaf-manifest.json' and 'The RESOURCE_MAP below emits those exact leaf paths'. Actual: the manifest enumerates the whole 45-file corpus while RESOURCE_MAP emits 26; 19 manifest leaves are emitted by no intent, so the 'exact leaf paths' coherence the paragraph promises does not hold.
